units.previous_finding: The quoted terminology used for “factored import statement” is rendered with wording whose ordinary Hebrew sense is “split/divided”, while the surrounding explanation describes grouping imports into one parenthesized declaration. This creates a small but real terminology/semantic tension in a basic Go syntax lesson. Revise the Hebrew terminology so the “factored” concept is clear and does not suggest the opposite grouping relationship.

The unit repeatedly renders the source concept “return value(s)” using terminology different from the glossary’s approved preferred mapping. There is no contextual reason in this unit requiring a different term. Align the terminology with the current Hebrew glossary while preserving the distinctions among named return values, bare/naked return, and the `return` keyword.

The title “ערימה של defers” uses an English-inflected plural of the Go keyword inside otherwise Hebrew prose. It is understandable, but it is not natural professional Hebrew and weakens the technical identity of the actual keyword `defer`. Revise the title so the stacking relationship is expressed naturally in Hebrew while preserving `defer` as the Go technical identity.

The linked Hebrew noun for “documentation” is preceded by the construction “ה־”, producing an unnatural Hebrew definite-article form before an already-Hebrew word. This is an RTL/orthographic presentation defect rather than a link-target problem. Revise the surrounding Hebrew so the definite article and linked Hebrew text read naturally without changing the link binding or `append` identity.

The source explicitly uses “return values”, but the candidate again uses terminology different from the glossary’s approved preferred mapping for `return value`. Align this teaching sentence with the current glossary terminology while preserving the distinction between function arguments and returned values.

The core definition of a closure contains clear Hebrew grammatical defects. The feminine noun for “closure” is paired with a masculine copular pronoun, and the clause describing assignment to referenced variables uses an invalid/non-natural verbal construction derived from the noun for “assignment”. These defects occur in the page's central technical definition and make the sentence unsuitable for direct publication. Revise the Hebrew grammar and assignment clause while preserving the source semantics and the identities `adder` and `sum`.

The natural-language occurrence of “struct” is left as the English token `struct`, despite the current glossary's mandatory Hebrew terminology for this teaching concept. It is not a protected code occurrence in this sentence. Align the prose with the mandatory glossary terminology without altering actual Go identifiers or code.

The title leaves the ordinary natural-language term “Receivers” in English while the body uses a Hebrew term for the same concept, creating an unnecessary mixed-language terminology inconsistency. The body also contains a Hebrew prefix joined with maqaf to an already-Hebrew noun in a way that is orthographically unnatural. Make the receiver terminology and Hebrew prefixing internally consistent while preserving pointer syntax such as `*T` and `*Vertex`.

The prose repeatedly uses Hebrew prefixes with maqaf before the Hebrew noun for receiver (`כ־…`, `ה־…`). That construction is appropriate around many LTR/foreign tokens but is unnatural when the following word is ordinary Hebrew. Normalize the Hebrew orthography without changing the technical distinction between value receivers and pointer receivers.

The same Hebrew-prefix problem appears in the phrase describing a value receiver: a Hebrew prefix is separated by maqaf from an already-Hebrew noun. Correct the Hebrew orthography while preserving the explanation of value-versus-pointer receiver behavior and all code identities.

Normalize both without changing `*Vertex`, `Scale`, `Abs`, or other protected technical identities.

The source explicitly uses “return value”, but the candidate uses terminology different from the glossary's approved preferred mapping, matching the same terminology inconsistency identified in group 1. There is no contextual need for a different term here. Align this occurrence with the current glossary while preserving `Rectangle`, `Bounds`, and `image.Rectangle`.

Select one consistent Hebrew grammatical treatment for the kept technical token across the unit while preserving the literal spelling and case of `goroutine` / `Goroutines`.

The rendering of “typed conduit” as `צינור מתויג־טיפוס` is non-idiomatic Hebrew and can suggest “type-tagged” rather than accurately explaining that a channel is a typed communication conduit. Revise this localized technical description for naturalness and semantic precision while retaining the mandatory channel terminology and `<-` operator identity.
